comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C99-C101 regarding speculative mechanisms involving cholesterol/lipid interactions. Both evaluations classify these as UNCERTAIN/speculative, noting lack of direct experimental evidence. Reviewers explicitly request further investigation of these proposals.

Both address claims C115-C117 about T cell hybridoma system limitations. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED (appropriately cautious acknowledgment), while peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN/concern, with all three reviewers emphasizing need for primary T cell validation. Significant disagreement on adequacy of current model system.

High overlap on evolutionary conservation claims C5, C39-C41, C80-C81. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes phylogenetic methodology and FEL analysis, while peer reviewers acknowledge evolutionary conservation as context for functional studies rather than primary contribution.

Strong agreement on claims C43-C55 regarding phosphorylation data showing CD4-pMHCII effects at high ligand density. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer R3 explicitly acknowledges these results and notes that proximal phosphorylation is insufficient for IL-2 production.

Both address main conclusions C10, C34, C82-C83, C91, C105, C107 about CD4 signaling independent of LCK. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers provide strong endorsement with all three reviewers acknowledging this as key finding that challenges classical model.

Overlap on claims C11-C12, C38, C97-C98, C109 regarding motif-dependent CD4 function. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval groups these with broader conclusions, while peer reviewers specifically highlight the two conserved motifs (GGXXG and palmitoylation) as central findings.

Overlap on claims C35-C37, C61, C77 about motif mutations reducing signaling. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative data from multiple cell lines, while peer reviewers integrate these findings into broader acceptance of motif importance.

Overlap on claims C75-C76, C78-C79 regarding signal amplification role of motifs. Both rate as SUPPORTED. These provide complementary evidence for motif function that both evaluations accept without challenge.

Overlap on claims C30-C33 about maintained pCD3ζ levels despite loss of CD4-LCK interaction. Both rate as SUPPORTED. This represents core experimental evidence that directly challenges prevailing model, strongly endorsed by peer reviewers.

Overlap on claims C56-C57, C59 regarding biochemical evidence for motif function independent of CD4-LCK association. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept these as mechanistic support for main conclusions.

Both address claims C69-C71 about ligand density effects and partial compensation by CD4-pMHCII binding. Both rate as SUPPORTED. These findings demonstrate context-dependent motif function accepted by both evaluations.

Overlap on claims C58, C60 regarding sucrose gradient data showing no change in residual CD4-LCK association. Both rate as SUPPORTED. These biochemical controls support independence of motif function from LCK binding.

Overlap on claims C61, C64, C68 about motifs functioning independently of CD4-LCK interactions. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes IL-2 production data, while peer reviewers integrate into broader motif function narrative.

Minimal overlap on claim C13 connecting evolutionary and mechanistic findings. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval discusses threshold model, while peer reviewers focus on evolutionary conservation as context.

Minimal overlap on claim C92 about quantitative reduction to ~16% pCD3ζ. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this as strong evidence for motif importance, peer reviewers accept within broader findings.
Minimal overlap on claims C72-C73 regarding ligand density dependence. Both rate as SUPPORTED. These complement primary findings about motif function under different stimulation conditions.

OpenEval R1 addresses foundational claims C1-C4, C17-C21 about CD4+ T cell receptor structure and function from literature. Rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these represent background context rather than novel findings.

OpenEval R3 addresses claims C22-C27 about prevailing model and prior challenges to it. Rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these provide historical context for the study's rationale.

OpenEval R12 addresses claims C102-C104 citing prior work on covariation and functional counterbalancing between CD4 motifs. Rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these cite previous literature for context.

OpenEval R13 addresses claims C106, C108, C110-C114 about alternative explanations for CD4-LCK interactions from literature. Rated SUPPORTED as appropriately speculative discussion. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R15 addresses claims C14-C16 about translational relevance to CAR-T therapy. Rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these provide translational context rather than experimental findings.

OpenEval R16 addresses claims C118-C121 describing experimental system characteristics. Rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are methodological details rather than findings requiring peer assessment.
